security_feature_bypassed: CTRL_AUX_REGWEN one-way write protection of the AES auxiliary control register, which lets trusted boot code permanently freeze the side-channel-related AES configuration until the next reset
finding: The write-enable gating term for the shadowed AES auxiliary control register is absent. src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:1038 assigns ctrl_aux_shadowed_gated_we = ctrl_aux_shadowed_we with no AND against the lock bit, so CTRL_AUX_REGWEN gates nothing, and that one qualifier feeds the write enable of both AUX fields at lines 1052 and 1088. How far this departs from the design's own convention is measurable inside the tree: 33 REGWEN write-enable gating assignments exist across four register blocks, 32 have the form '<reg>_gated_we = <reg>_we & <regwen>_qs' (for example kmac_reg_top.sv:554 for an equally shadowed register, and csrng_reg_top.sv:631), and this line is the only exception. It is also the only one of the 33 sites lacking the register generator's fixed marker comment, and the only single-line always_comb in the entire tree. The lock signal ctrl_aux_regwen_qs is still declared at line 223, still driven by its caliptra_prim_subreg instance at line 1136, and still readable over MMIO at line 1823, so software sees a lock that reads back as engaged while having no effect on the write path. The register block's own specification contradicts the RTL: src/aes/data/aes.rdl:181-188 documents that once the bit is cleared to 0 the auxiliary control register 'cannot be written anymore', and aes_reg_top.sv carries the header 'Register Top module auto-generated by reggen' from that RDL. The lock is instantiated as SwAccessW0C with RESVAL 1'h1 at line 1115, so a single write of 0 engages it irreversibly until reset, which is precisely the state the bypass defeats. The affected field with a live effect in this build is KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED, which src/aes/rtl/aes_control_fsm.sv:1120 uses to gate prng_reseed_we_o when a new key is loaded. The register's other field, FORCE_MASKS, is writable but inert here because aes.sv:24 defaults SecAllowForcingMasks to 0 and aes_clp_wrapper.sv:309 instantiates aes with no override, so no impact is claimed for it.
detection_method: LLM-driven CSBC analysis of the audited RTL, confirmed against the register block's own RDL specification and against the design's own write-enable gating convention, then hardened with a 33-gate structural witness whose decisive gate is a computed tree-wide census (33 REGWEN gating assignments, 32 gated, 1 not, and the ungated one is the audited line), a directed VCS simulation of aes_reg_top over TL-UL, and a negative control in which the tree's own gating idiom is applied to that line in a scratch copy and the identical testbench is required to fail
security_impact: Privileged software at supervisor mode can modify the AES auxiliary security configuration after that configuration has been locked, defeating a protection whose whole purpose is to be irreversible. Concretely, KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED can be cleared from its secure default of 1 to 0 while the lock reads back as engaged; loading a new AES key then no longer reseeds the masking and clearing PRNGs, so masking randomness carries across key changes and the first-order side-channel countermeasure is weakened. Because the lock still reads back as 0, software and any attestation logic that inspects it are misled into believing the configuration is frozen. Turning the weakened countermeasure into AES key recovery would additionally require power or electromagnetic measurement access to the device; this submission proves the RTL-level bypass and the degraded reseeding, not the final trace-based recovery step.
proposed_mitigation: Add the gating term in src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:1038 so the write enable is ANDed with the lock, matching the form used by the other 32 gating sites in this tree: assign ctrl_aux_shadowed_gated_we = ctrl_aux_shadowed_we & ctrl_aux_regwen_qs; and regenerate the file from src/aes/data/aes.rdl rather than editing it by hand, so the RTL cannot drift from the RDL contract again.

Add a lint or CI rule that fails when a REGWEN-class signal is declared and read back over MMIO but drives no write-enable term, since that combination produces a lock that appears functional to software while gating nothing.
Add an assertion that CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED never changes value while CTRL_AUX_REGWEN reads 0, and bind it wherever the AES register block is integrated.

Add a regression test that locks CTRL_AUX_REGWEN, attempts two shadow writes to CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED, and fails if KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED changes, using the testbench in this submission (proof/tb/aes_reg_bug_003_tb.sv) together with its negative control (proof/logs/negative_control.log).
exploit_or_attack_flow: After reset, CTRL_AUX_REGWEN reads 1 (unlocked) and CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED.KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED holds its secure default of 1, so loading a new AES key reseeds the masking and clearing PRNGs.

Trusted boot software writes 0 to CTRL_AUX_REGWEN at offset 0x7c to freeze the auxiliary configuration. The bit is SwAccessW0C, so this is irreversible until the next reset, and a read back confirms 0x0.
The attacker, running later at supervisor mode, issues two consecutive MMIO writes of 0x0 to CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED at offset 0x78, satisfying the shadow register's two-write commit protocol.

Because aes_reg_top.sv:1038 passes the write enable through ungated, both writes are accepted and the shadow register commits. KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED becomes 0 and shadowed_update_err is never asserted, so nothing reports the violation.

The attacker loads a new AES key. aes_control_fsm.sv:1120 no longer asserts prng_reseed_we_o on the key-init pulse, so the masking PRNG is not reseeded and its randomness carries over from the previous key.

Verified in simulation: REGWEN reads 0x1 after reset and 0x0 after the lock, while KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED moves 1 to 0 under the engaged lock, with shadowed_update_err staying low. With this tree's own gating idiom applied to that line in a scratch copy, the identical testbench observes the field unchanged at 1 and its cover counter falls to 0, while its control checks still pass, confirming the observation is specific to this RTL rather than to a broken harness.
